title: Medical Records Retrieval: How It Works, What It Costs, How Long It Takes
summary: Medical records retrieval means obtaining a claimant's actual charts from the providers who treated them, under a signed HIPAA authorization or subpoena. The 30-day deadline most guides cite doesn't apply to third-party requests — which is why carrier and law-firm requests run 30 to 90 days, sometimes longer.
body_text: Medical record retrieval is the step where a claim stops running on assumptions. A canvass tells you a claimant was treated somewhere. The records tell you what was actually diagnosed, when, and by whom. That is what a compensability decision, an apportionment argument, or a fraud referral finally rests on. It is also the step most likely to sit open for months while nobody can say why. TL;DR Medical records retrieval is the process of obtaining a claimant's or plaintiff's actual medical charts from the providers who treated them. It requires a signed HIPAA authorization or a subpoena — unlike a medical canvass , which only confirms whether and where treatment happened. The 30-day HIPAA deadline nearly every guide cites applies to patients requesting their own records under 45 CFR § 164.524. It does not apply to third-party requests made under a § 164.508 authorization — the kind carriers, TPAs, and law firms actually send. Those carry no federal deadline at all. In practice: 7–14 days from a small practice, 30–60 from a hospital system, and 90 days or more from a large integrated system. Cost is a per-request retrieval fee plus per-page copying charges, and since Ciox Health, LLC v. Azar (2020) the federal fee caps no longer protect third-party requesters. The single largest variable in your timeline is not the provider. It is how often somebody follows up. What Medical Records Retrieval Is, and What It Isn't Records retrieval is the act of requesting, chasing, obtaining, and verifying a complete set of medical records from a specific provider for a specific person over a specific date range. It gets confused with three neighbouring things, and the distinction matters because each has a different legal basis and a different price: Process What you get What it requires Typical cost basis Medical canvass Whether, when, and where treatment occurred Nothing — no PHI is disclosed Per location contacted Records retrieval The actual charts, notes, imaging reports, billing Signed authorization or subpoena Per request + per page Record summary / review A narrative or chronology built from the charts The records already in hand Per page or per hour IME An independent physician's opinion Scheduling and examination Per examination The sequence matters. Canvassing first, retrieval second, examination last, because each step narrows the expense of the next. We covered the ordering logic in detail in medical canvassing vs. records retrieval vs. IME ; the short version is that retrieving records from forty providers because you don't know which one treated the claimant is the most expensive possible way to answer a question a canvass answers for a fraction of the cost. Retrieval is also not a single transaction. It is a campaign. That framing explains most of what goes wrong with it. What You Need Before You Can Request Anything There are exactly three lawful routes to another person's medical records, and picking the wrong one restarts your clock. A HIPAA authorization signed by the patient. This is the workhorse for claims work. Under 45 CFR § 164.508, a valid authorization has to contain six elements: a description of the information to be disclosed, who is authorized to disclose it, who is authorized to receive it, the purpose, an expiration date or triggering event, and the patient's signature and date. Miss one and the provider is entitled to reject it. Many will, after sitting on it for three weeks first. A subpoena or court order. Slower and more expensive, but it does not depend on the claimant's cooperation. Some providers, particularly large systems and behavioural health facilities, will insist on one regardless of what authorization you hold. A state-specific form. Several states, and a great many individual health systems, require their own release form rather than a generic one. This is the single most common avoidable rejection: a technically valid HIPAA authorization returned because the custodian wants their own paperwork. Two categories of record carry extra protection almost everywhere and need explicit, separate consent: substance use disorder treatment records under 42 CFR Part 2, and mental health or psychotherapy notes. A general authorization does not reach them. If your claim involves either, plan for a second request. The Six Steps of a Retrieval Request Identify the provider precisely. Not "the orthopedist in Tampa," but the legal entity name, the correct location, and the fax number the records department actually monitors. Practices merge, relocate, and rebrand constantly, and a request sent to a closed location simply vanishes. Confirm who the custodian is. The treating physician does not control record release. The custodian does, and at a hospital that is the Health Information Management department, not the clinic you called. Submit with the right paperwork. Correct authorization or subpoena, correct form, correct date range, correct channel. Most providers still prefer fax. Follow up. Repeatedly. This is the step that determines your turnaround, and it is the step almost every workflow under-resources. Receive and pay. Records arrive with an invoice for retrieval and copying. Payment is often a precondition of release. Verify completeness. Check the date range you asked for against the date range you received. Partial productions are extremely common and, if unnoticed, quietly undermine whatever decision you build on them. Step 6 gets skipped under time pressure more than any other, and it is the one that costs the most later. A chart that stops six weeks before the date you actually needed is worse than no chart, because it looks like an answer. Who the Records Custodian Is, and Why They Control Your Timeline A medical records custodian is the person or department legally responsible for maintaining and releasing a provider's records. At a solo practice it may be the office manager. At a hospital it is the HIM department. Increasingly, and this is the layer most requesters never learn about, it is an outsourced release-of-information vendor working under contract to the provider. That third case changes your economics. An outsourced ROI vendor has its own fee schedule, its own turnaround targets, and no relationship with you. It processes requests in the order received and has no particular incentive to expedite yours. Knowing which of the three you are dealing with before you send the request is worth more than any amount of chasing afterward. It tells you what form to use, what fee to expect, and whether a phone call will accomplish anything at all. How Long It Actually Takes Here is where most guidance on this topic is confidently wrong. The widely repeated rule is that HIPAA gives a provider 30 days, extendable once by 30 more. That rule is real, and it lives at 45 CFR § 164.524. But it governs an individual's right to access their own records. The requests carriers, TPAs, and law firms send are third-party disclosures under § 164.508, and the regulation sets no response deadline for those at all. The authorization specifies an expiration date; it does not specify how fast the provider has to act. So the honest answer is that there is no federal clock on your request. Some states impose their own deadlines, typically 15 to 30 days, and those do bind. Absent a state rule, you are relying on the custodian's workload and your own persistence. Provider type Typical turnaround Why Small practice (1–5 providers) 7–14 days One person handles it; a phone call reaches them Urgent care 10–20 days Often centralized across locations Imaging centre 10–21 days Reports fast; actual studies slower Hospital system 30–60 days HIM department queue, frequently outsourced Large integrated system 60–90+ days High volume, strict process, no expediting Behavioural health / SUD 45–90+ days 42 CFR Part 2 consent, often needs a subpoena Six months is not a horror story; it is a normal outcome at a large integrated system when nobody chases the request. And the reason is unglamorous. A request that receives one follow-up call every two weeks sits behind every request that receives one every other day, because queue position at a busy HIM department is substantially a function of who is asking. What It Costs A retrieval invoice has two or three components: A retrieval or processing fee , generally $20–75 per request, charged by the provider or its ROI vendor. Per-page copying charges , capped by state statute in most states, typically structured as a higher rate for the first tranche of pages and a lower rate thereafter. A 300-page hospital chart can produce copying charges well in excess of the retrieval fee. Certification or affidavit fees , where you need a custodian-of-records affidavit for litigation use. The federal fee caps do not help you here. In Ciox Health, LLC v. Azar , 435 F. Supp. 3d 30 (D.D.C. 2020), the court held that the fee limitation at 45 CFR § 164.524(c)(4), including the $6.50 flat-fee option for electronic copies, applies only to an individual requesting their own records, not to requests to transmit records to a third party. Providers and ROI vendors are therefore free to charge more than cost on the requests claims organizations actually make. That ruling is a large part of why third-party retrieval costs what it does. One pricing detail worth pinning down in any vendor contract: most vendors bill for attempts , not successes. If 45% of requests ultimately produce records, a quoted per-request fee understates your real cost per obtained chart by more than double. Ask how "successful retrieval" is defined, in writing, before volume ramps. Where Retrieval Breaks Down Across claims organizations the same four failures recur, and none of them are really about the provider. Inconsistent follow-up. The dominant cause of long timelines. Follow-up is unglamorous, easy to defer, and invisible until a file is 90 days old. No status visibility. A requester who cannot see that nothing has happened cannot escalate. Silence from a vendor reads identically to silence from a provider, and the file ages either way. Wrong paperwork, discovered late. A rejected authorization often surfaces three weeks in, and the clock restarts from zero. Unverified completeness. Partial records accepted as complete. The most expensive failure, because it is the one nobody catches. Notice that three of the four are follow-up and communication problems rather than access problems. The records were always obtainable. The process just didn't push. And yes, fax. Healthcare still runs on it, and any retrieval operation that cannot originate, receive, and confirm faxes at volume is working with one hand tied. Phone reaches a human, fax satisfies the custodian's process, email carries the authorization. A serious retrieval workflow uses all three, per provider, depending on what that provider actually responds to. How Superunit Handles Records Retrieval Superunit automates medical canvassing and records retrieval with AI agents working by phone, fax, and email. The effect is scale without staffing: outreach and follow-up run across every open file at once, and the cost of doing that is the same at four hundred requests as at forty. AI does not make a hospital HIM department move faster. Nothing does; that queue is set by their staffing and their process. What changes is the cadence on your side. An agent can re-contact every open request every other day rather than every second week. Every contact attempt is also logged and transcribed, so "we're still waiting on the facility" becomes a timestamped record of who was called, when, and what they said. For a claims manager holding a 60-day-old file, that is the difference between escalating and hoping. Where Human Investigators Still Win Automation is the wrong tool for several parts of this work, and pretending otherwise wastes everyone's time. Subpoena practice needs a person. Negotiating with a custodian who has decided to be difficult needs a person. Anything requiring physical presence, in-person credentialing, or judgment about a genuinely ambiguous record set needs a person. And where a client's master service agreement restricts AI involvement, which is common enough among large carriers to plan around, the work has to run through a human team regardless of capability. The realistic division is that agents carry the volume and the cadence, and humans carry the exceptions and the escalations. Most retrieval work is volume and cadence. Why Superunit Runs the Canvass First Retrieval is the second step, not the first. Sending requests to every provider in a radius because you don't know which one treated the claimant is how retrieval budgets get consumed without producing answers. Because Superunit runs both services, the canvass comes first — starting at $1.50 per location , roughly $45 for a standard 30-facility canvass — to establish where treatment actually happened. Records then get requested only from the providers that returned a hit, and the same parallel outreach that removes the headcount ceiling on canvassing carries the follow-up after it. How to Evaluate a Retrieval Vendor Most vendor comparisons in this category turn on price per request, which is the least useful number available. Five questions separate vendors more reliably: How is "successful retrieval" defined, and do you bill attempts or successes? Get it in writing. This single definition can double or halve your effective cost per obtained chart, and it is where invoice disputes originate. What is your follow-up cadence, and can I see it? Weekly follow-up and every-other-day follow-up produce materially different turnaround on the same request. A vendor who cannot state their cadence does not have one. How do I get status without asking? If checking on an open request requires an email from your team, your team is the status system. Proactive reporting on no-movement files is worth more than a marginally lower fee, because it is what lets you escalate before a file is 90 days old. Do provider fees pass through at cost, or are they marked up? Retrieval fees and statutory copying charges are the larger part of many invoices. A low headline rate with marked-up pass-throughs is more expensive than a higher rate at cost. What is the audit trail? For anything heading toward litigation, you need to show what was requested, when, from whom, and what came back. Vendors vary enormously here, and the gap only becomes visible in a deposition. Two structural questions matter at volume. Ask whether pricing changes between 40 requests a month and 400. A vendor whose model is staffed by headcount will price the second tier much higher, and one whose model isn't, won't. And ask about coverage outside your core geography, including Puerto Rico and international providers, which routinely appear in claims files and routinely stall vendors who have no process for them. Frequently Asked Questions Do I need a signed authorization for records retrieval? Yes. An authorization meeting the six requirements of 45 CFR § 164.508, a subpoena, or a court order. There is no route to a third party's medical records without one of the three. A medical canvass requires none of them, because it discloses no PHI. Does HIPAA's 30-day rule apply to my request? Almost certainly not. The 30-day rule at 45 CFR § 164.524 covers an individual requesting their own records. Third-party requests under an authorization have no federal deadline. Check your state — many impose one of 15 to 30 days. Why do some providers demand a subpoena when I already have an authorization? Providers may impose stricter requirements than HIPAA's floor, and many do as a matter of policy, particularly large systems and behavioural health facilities. It is their prerogative, and arguing rarely moves it faster than complying. What does records retrieval cost? A retrieval fee of roughly $20–75 per request plus state-capped per-page copying charges, and certification fees where an affidavit is needed. The federal fee caps do not apply to third-party requests after Ciox v. Azar . Can AI retrieve medical records? AI can prepare and submit requests, follow up across phone, fax, and email, and report status. It cannot compel a provider to respond faster than that provider's process allows. The gain is in cadence and coverage, not in the provider's speed. What is a records custodian? The person or department legally responsible for releasing a provider's records: an office manager at a small practice, the HIM department at a hospital, or an outsourced release-of-information vendor. The custodian, not the treating physician, controls whether and when your request is fulfilled. Sources Individuals' Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information, 45 CFR § 164.524 — HHS.gov 45 CFR § 164.524 — Access of individuals to protected health information (eCFR) Ciox Health, LLC v. Azar, 435 F. Supp. 3d 30 (D.D.C. 2020) Federal Court Strikes Down HIPAA Fee Limitations for Third-Party Medical Records Requests — Dinsmore

title: How to Put a Cartoon Character Into a Real Video With AI
summary: Put a cartoon character into real video with AI for free. Learn how to replace people with cartoon characters using Magic Hour in 2026.
body_text: Quick Answer Magic Hour's Character Replace tool lets you replace the main person in an existing video with a cartoon, anime, illustration, or other character using a reference image. You upload the source video and character image, and the AI keeps the original timing, poses, body movement, and camera motion while changing the subject. You get 3 free generations per day , with each free generation limited to 3 seconds . The browser-based workflow lets you start without signing up, making it different from cartoon video generators that create an entirely new scene from a prompt. Intro A brand mascot can deliver a product demo, an educational character can present a lesson, or a fictional persona can become the face of a YouTube channel. Creating that kind of video traditionally means animating the character from scratch, which can take time, software, and technical skills. With AI character replacement, you can instead take an existing video and replace the person in it with a cartoon character while keeping the original performance. TL;DR Find or create a cartoon character reference image. Open Magic Hour's Character Replace tool; no sign-up is required to start. Upload your real video and cartoon reference image, then click Generate . The cartoon character follows the original video's movements, timing, and camera motion. Free users can generate clips up to 3 seconds. Paid users can generate up to 15 seconds. Generating Cartoons vs Replacing Characters: What's the Difference? There are two different ways to make a cartoon video with AI. One generates an entirely new scene, while the other starts with footage you already have and changes the character inside it. Approach How It Works Best For Generate cartoon from scratch Type a prompt and AI creates a new cartoon video When you have no existing footage and want a fully animated scene Replace character in real video Upload existing footage and a cartoon reference, then AI replaces the person When you have real footage and want a specific cartoon character to perform it This guide covers the second approach using Magic Hour's Character Replace tool. What You Can Make With This Workflow Brand mascot videos: Have a brand mascot deliver a product demo, advertisement, or explainer without building an animation workflow from scratch. Educational content: Put a cartoon character into classroom, tutorial, or presentation footage to make lessons more engaging. Faceless YouTube channels: Use a cartoon persona instead of appearing on camera yourself. Social media content: Let a mascot or original cartoon character perform a trending video format while keeping the original motion. Personal creative projects: Create fan videos, funny clips, or character-driven social content using footage you already have. Magic Hour specifically supports stylized references such as cartoons, anime, and illustrations, while preserving the source clip's performance and scene. Where to Get Your Cartoon Character Reference Image The hardest part of this workflow may actually happen before you open the video tool: finding a good cartoon reference image. You have three straightforward options. Option 1: Use a Built-In Preset Magic Hour's Character Replace page currently includes 10 presets: Deadpool, Kratos, Chun-Li, Peter Griffin, Robot, Keanu Reeves, Elmo, Walter White, Stormtrooper, and The Grinch . This is the easiest way to test the workflow because you do not need to find or prepare another image. Peter Griffin, Elmo, and The Grinch are also useful for seeing how a recognizable cartoon or stylized character translates into existing footage. For commercial projects, however, remember that having access to a character preset does not automatically give you the rights to use that character commercially. See the copyright section below. Option 2: Use Your Own Brand Mascot or Original Character If your company already has a mascot, or you have designed your own cartoon character, this is usually the cleanest option. For the reference image, look for: A clear, front-facing character Good lighting and sharp details A simple or uncluttered background Clearly visible facial features Distinctive shapes, colors, and clothing Magic Hour recommends using a sharp, well-lit reference where the character is clearly visible with minimal obstruction. A simple character sheet or clean illustration can therefore be more useful than a highly detailed image with lots of background elements. Option 3: Generate a Custom Cartoon Character You can also create an original character first with Magic Hour's AI Image Generator , then use that image as the Character Replace reference. Try prompts such as: flat design cartoon character, blue outfit, bold black outlines, front-facing, simple white background Or: friendly cartoon brand mascot, round shape, yellow and blue color palette, bold black outlines, front-facing, clean vector style Or: original cartoon presenter, green jacket, expressive face, simple flat illustration, bold outlines, front-facing, plain background The advantage of this route is that you can design a character specifically for your project instead of trying to adapt an existing IP. What You Need Before You Start You only need a few things: A real video featuring a person: A short clip with clear lighting and a visible subject is a good starting point. Magic Hour's Character Replace currently supports clips up to 15 seconds in the full create workflow. A cartoon reference image: Use one of the presets above or prepare your own image. A modern browser: Magic Hour's browser-based tools work across common desktop and mobile browsers. No account to start: Eligible free Magic Hour tools provide daily generations without requiring sign-up, while the full signed-in Create workflow uses credits. How the Main Tools Compare If your goal is specifically to put a cartoon character into existing footage, the important distinction is whether the tool can work from your video + character reference , rather than only generating a new video. Tool Free Without Sign-Up Puts Cartoon Into Real Footage Custom Character Upload Works in Browser No Watermark Free Magic Hour Yes Yes Yes Yes Free preview/testing; paid plans remove watermark Viggle AI No Yes, through Mix/motion workflows Yes Yes No Loova AI No Yes Yes Yes Not clearly stated for the free tier Pika No Yes Yes Yes No Runway No Limited for this exact workflow Yes Yes No Magic Hour stands out by focusing specifically on replacing the primary subject in an existing video while preserving the original scene and motion, whereas tools like Viggle, Pika, and Runway take broader approaches to character animation, video editing, and generation. How to Put a Cartoon Character Into a Real Video: Step by Step Step 1: Prepare Your Cartoon Reference Image Start with a clear cartoon image where the character is easy to see. A front-facing image with good lighting, minimal obstruction, and a simple background gives the AI more useful visual information to work with. You can use a built-in preset, upload your own mascot or original character, or generate one with Magic Hour's AI Image Generator. Step 2: Go to Magic Hour's Character Replace Tool Open the Magic Hour Character Replace tool . The product page provides a simple three-part workflow: Add video → Add image → Generate , and you can start without creating an account. Step 3: Upload Your Video and Cartoon Reference Upload the real video you want to transform, then add your cartoon reference image. If you want to test the workflow quickly, choose one of the built-in presets instead of uploading a separate image. For the source footage, avoid clips with heavy motion blur, very dark lighting, frequent cuts, or a subject who is heavily blocked by other objects. Magic Hour specifically notes that low light, motion blur, heavy occlusion, and fast cuts can contribute to flicker or drift. Step 4: Generate Click Generate and let Magic Hour process the clip. For videos under 15 seconds, generation typically takes less than 5 minutes . The tool keeps the source video's timing, body movement, poses, and camera motion while replacing the primary subject. Step 5: Review and Download When the result is ready, watch the full clip before downloading it. Check whether the cartoon character stays recognizable, whether the movement remains stable, and whether the original background still looks natural. Magic Hour says Character Replace keeps the original scene and background while changing the primary subject. If the first result is not quite right, try another reference image or preset rather than rebuilding the entire source video. Tips for the Most Natural Result Start with a simple cartoon design. Flat colors and bold outlines generally give the AI clearer visual features to work with than highly detailed illustrations. Use slower or medium-paced footage first. Fast movement gives the model less visual information per frame and can make character details harder to maintain. Keep the source background relatively simple. A clean background makes the replacement character easier to distinguish from surrounding objects. Use even lighting. Bright, consistent lighting helps separate the original subject from the background and reduces the conditions that can contribute to flicker or drift. Make the character's silhouette distinctive. For cartoons, a strong outline, recognizable hairstyle, large accessories, or a simple color palette can make the replacement easier to read than a character with many tiny details. The biggest takeaway is that the reference image matters just as much as the source video. If the character is difficult to identify in the still image, the same problem can become more noticeable once it is moving. A Note on Copyright Technically, an AI tool can accept a reference image of a recognizable cartoon character, but that does not mean you have permission to use the character commercially. Using copyrighted characters from companies such as Disney or Nickelodeon in commercial content generally requires the appropriate rights or license. For commercial projects, the safer approach is to use an original character you created yourself or a character you have properly licensed. For personal, clearly non-commercial fan content, the situation can vary depending on the country, platform, and specific use, so check the rules that apply to your project. What to Try Next Once your cartoon character is in the footage, you can make it speak using Magic Hour's Lip Sync tool , which can synchronize the character's mouth with new audio. If you want to transform the whole video into a cartoon-like visual style instead of replacing only the person, try Magic Hour's Video-to-Video tool . Both workflows start with existing footage, but they solve different problems: Character Replace changes the main subject, while Video-to-Video changes the visual treatment of the footage. Frequently Asked Questions Can I use any cartoon character as the reference image, including copyrighted ones? The Character Replace workflow supports stylized references such as cartoons, anime, and illustrations, so the tool can technically work with many different character images. However, permission to upload an image is different from permission to use the resulting character commercially. For commercial content, use an original or properly licensed character. Will the cartoon style look natural in a real video? The result depends heavily on both the cartoon reference and the source footage. Clean, flat-design characters with strong outlines are generally easier to read in motion, while highly detailed illustrations can make inconsistencies more noticeable. Magic Hour also recommends sharp, well-lit references and warns that fast cuts, motion blur, low light, and heavy occlusion can make flicker or drift more likely. Is it free? If you don't sign up: You can try Magic Hour's Character Replace directly from the product page with up to 3 free generations per day , making it useful for testing the workflow before creating an account. If you sign in: Character Replace uses credits based on the clip and settings. For example, a 15-second clip currently costs 720 credits in 480p or 1,440 credits in 720p in the full Create workflow, with shorter clips costing less. Paid plans provide larger credit allocations and remove the watermark. Does it work for a character I designed myself, not a famous cartoon? Yes. Character Replace accepts a reference image, so you can upload your own mascot, original cartoon, or AI-generated character as long as the image clearly shows the subject. This is also a practical choice for commercial content because you can control the rights to an original character instead of relying on someone else's IP. What happens to my uploaded video after generation? Magic Hour says uploaded content has a one-day retention period and that uploads and outputs are not used to train its models. You can also delete your content or account at any time, with deletion removing content from active storage immediately.

title: How to decorate your virtual office for the holidays

body_text: Decorating for the season or holidays is an easy way to delight your team and bring fresh energy to your virtual workspace. Imagine everyone’s surprise when a pumpkin appears on their desk, or everything turns green for St. Patrick’s Day! Plus, part of the benefit of a virtual office is that you can decorate it however you want, whenever you want, with minimal setup and takedown time. title: How Vuetify Cut API Response Times to 50ms With Cosmic
summary: Vuetify, the Vue component library with over 4 million monthly npm downloads, cut server response times from 300-400ms to about 50ms with Cosmic.
body_text: The team behind four million monthly downloads Vuetify has grown, since its founding in 2016, into one of the leading component libraries for building Vue applications. The package recorded 4,114,254 npm downloads in the 30 days ending August 3, 2026. It is led by founder and CEO John Leider, and the team's focus has always been on building systems that are intuitive and easy to use. When Vuetify went looking for a content API, they held their own tooling to that same standard. The problem: a slow Shopify back end and content living in the codebase In early 2020, Vuetify was dealing with two things at once. The first was the online store. It was completely integrated into Shopify's back-end platform, and getting that API to communicate with the front end of the website was far too slow. Rendering a page required too many queries. The second was the cost of growth. Vuetify's rapid expansion left the team managing all different kinds of documents, affiliate links, and sponsors inside their original code base. Every content update was a code change, reviewed and deployed like a feature. For a team whose actual product is a component library, that was quickly becoming sub-optimal. Vuetify needed an API that matched their appreciation for intuitive design and included the flexible features they required. After evaluating their options, nothing seemed like the right combination of those values, except for Cosmic. The result: 300-400 ms down to about 50 ms It was literally 10 to 15 minutes from taking the SDK, to getting the data I needed, to consuming it. We cut our server response time down from 300-400 ms to about 50 ms. Instead of needing to query the Shopify API, now we only need to query Cosmic. The baseline just works out-of-the-box, and there's considerable more information and documentation if you need it. John Leider, Chief Executive Officer, Vuetify Three concrete outcomes sit in that quote: Server response time dropped from 300-400 ms to about 50 ms. Measured against the top of the original range, that is roughly an 85% reduction. Integration took 10 to 15 minutes , from installing the SDK to consuming live data on the front end. One API replaced two. Product content that previously required Shopify API calls now comes back from a single Cosmic query. The full story is on the Vuetify customer page . Why Cosmic fit The API surface matched the existing stack. Cosmic exposes a REST API and a JavaScript SDK, both of which drop into Vue and plain JavaScript projects without ceremony. There is no proprietary runtime to adopt, no separate deployment layer, and no framework requirement. The team models its own content. Object types and metafields are defined in the Cosmic dashboard, so adding a field to a sponsor record or restructuring a document type does not require a developer or a release. Fewer round trips per page. Consolidating content behind a single API removed the multi-query pattern that made the original integration slow. That consolidation is where the 50 ms figure comes from. What Vuetify keeps in Cosmic Cosmic holds the content that used to be split between Shopify's back end and Vuetify's repository: store and product content, sponsor placements, affiliate links, and the assorted documents a fast-growing open-source project accumulates. Moving that material into a content API changes the unit of work. Adding a sponsor or correcting an affiliate link becomes a dashboard edit that is live immediately, with no pull request, review cycle, or deploy attached to it. What the integration looks like Reading content from Cosmic in a Vue or Nuxt project takes a few lines: That is the entire integration surface. The SDK handles authentication, query construction, and typing of the response. There is no CMS runtime to host and no custom content server to keep alive. Why this pattern holds for developer-facing teams Vuetify's setup generalizes well to any project where the content and the code evolve at different speeds. Documentation, changelogs, sponsor pages, and marketing copy all change more often than the library itself, and each of those changes carries no engineering risk. Routing them through a content API keeps them out of the release process, which frees maintainer time for the library. Open source has a particular version of this constraint. As John Leider put it in his developer spotlight interview way back in 2019 , the hard part of OSS is that "the supply does not always meet the demand," which forces teams to be efficient about where their hours go. Content operations are a good place to reclaim some. Start building Cosmic is free to start: 1 Bucket, 2 team members, and 1,000 Objects on the Free plan, with no credit card required. title: Live Updates: Trump Administration Tariffs, Trade Policy Changes, and Impacts on Global Supply Chains
summary: Discover Flexport APIs and EDIs to speed, scale, and optimize your supply chain. Developer tools make it easy to instantly access logistics data and vital cargo and global trade documentation in the Flexport Platform or your ERP.
body_text: New Section 232 tariffs on drones take effect September 3 President Trump signed a proclamation on August 13, Adjusting Imports of Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Unmanned Aircraft Systems Components into the United States , placing Section 232 duties on unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), better known as drones, plus their parts, docking stations, and chargers. Rates take effect September 3, 2026. What you pay depends on how much the drone weighs, what sensors it carries, and what it's used for. The covered Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) codes are listed in Annex IV. What the rates look like 25% on small drones, meaning a takeoff weight of 25 kg or less, but only those without thermal imaging. 100% on any drone above 25 kg takeoff weight, and on small drones that carry thermal imaging. 100% on docking stations and chargers, regardless of the size of the drone they serve. 100% on a defined list of drone parts. Many of those parts carry a use restriction, so the HTS code flags the item, but the duty doesn't apply if the part isn't destined for a drone. A second group of parts, propellers and body components, moves to 25% on February 9. Who's excluded Parts headed for drones escape the duty if the drone itself is used for agriculture, retail delivery, or sale to the Department of War. Several of these exclusions expire after six months, though the expiry language in the proclamation carries the same date problem noted above. Capped rates come with a new certification test The United Kingdom gets a 10% cap. The European Union, Japan, Taiwan, Switzerland and Liechtenstein, and South Korea get 15%. Those caps aren't automatic. The proclamation applies them only where importers certify that "substantially all the critical components and technology" originate in the United States, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, an EU member nation, or the United Kingdom. The Secretary of Commerce will build the process for deciding which products meet that bar. "Substantially all critical components" is a brand new standard with no precedent to lean on. If you import finished drones from a capped country but source critical components elsewhere, don't assume you'll land at 10% or 15%. Will these stack with Section 301? The proclamation doesn't say. Flexport's customs team is filing on the assumption that the new Section 232 duties won't stack with existing Section 301 tariffs, and we're watching for a Cargo Systems Messaging Service (CSMS) notice from U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), which typically arrives the day the tariffs go live. We'll update this post when CBP confirms. What importers should do now Pull your drone and drone-component HTS codes and check them against Annex IV. Weight and thermal imaging are the two variables that swing a shipment from 25% to 100%, so classification detail matters more than usual here. If you're planning to claim a capped country rate, start assembling component origin documentation now, because the certification process will require it. We're adding these rates to the Flexport Tariff Simulator and expect them live by Saturday, August 16. Set your entry date to September 3 or later to see the impact. Questions on how this hits your shipments? Reach out to your Flexport team or get in touch with a Flexport customs expert.

title: L3Harris Demonstrates Multi-Domain Supremacy at Annual Project Convergence Exercise
summary: L3Harris Technologies recently showcased a variety of interoperable, multi-domain capabilities at the Army’s Project Convergence-Capstone 6 at Fort Irwin, California.
body_text: MELBOURNE, Fla., Aug. 18, 2026 — L3Harris Technologies (NYSE: LHX) recently showcased a variety of interoperable, multi-domain capabilities at the Army’s Project Convergence-Capstone 6 at Fort Irwin, California. The company successfully linked decision makers with multi-domain sensors and effectors in unified networks for rapid interdiction of threats in complex and contested environments. L3Harris’ key capabilities included interoperable, multi-domain assured communications , Link 16 integration onto UH-60 Black Hawks, and the Deceptor™ modular electronic warfare payload. “Our wide range of open system defense technologies have modern, high-volume manufacturing and resilient supply chains to support their rapid delivery into the hands of soldiers,” said Christopher Aebli, President, Communications & Spectrum Dominance, L3Harris. “Many of the capabilities we demonstrated at Project Convergence show our technology is ready to meet the demands of tomorrow, providing additional value to the U.S. government’s investments into software-defined and open-systems solutions.” The company also teamed with ARX Robotics to provide an integrated, counter-unmanned aerial system capability leveraging L3Harris’ CORVUS-RAVEN . L3Harris is making continued progress in support of new Army requirements after its selection as a Next Generation Command and Control transport layer provider . The company also recently showcased its capabilities at Ivy Mass, Lightning Surge and Operation Jailbreak, where its Wraith® waveform and WESCAM® MX®-Series of electro-optical/infrared sensor systems were validated as “jailbroken.” About L3Harris Technologies L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security. Visit L3Harris.com for more information. # # # Media Contacts Jason Simpson Communications and Spectrum Dominance C: 863-338-9817 Jason.Simpson01@L3Harris.com Sara Banda Corporate Public Relations C: 321-306-8927 Media@L3Harris.com Related Capabilities Link 16 Tactical Data Links L3Harris Link 16 tactical data links and LOS comms provide enhanced situational awareness and reduced fratricide potential. Deceptor™ L3Harris' Deceptor™ is a radio frequency (RF) electronic warfare (EW) system based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware that leverages cutting-edge software capability. CORVUS-RAVEN Counter-Drone Capability CORVUS-RAVEN tactical counter-small uncrewed aircraft system (sUAS) brings operators passive signal detect capability, enhanced situational awareness and defeat jamming capability. AN/PRC-163 Multi-channel Handheld Radio Share voice, data and full motion video across networks for over 200 users. Dual-channel crossbanding. SWaP-optimized. TSM‑X MANET. NGC2: Enabling Next Generation Command and Control Radios that adapt. Waveforms that survive. Integration that keeps command and control alive when the spectrum is contested. Distributed Spectrum Collaboration and Operations (DiSCO™) DiSCO technology is a resilient, future-fit electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) architecture that weaponizes electronic warfare (EW) data to achieve overmatch at campaign speed. title: WeTouch Technology Inc. Reports First Half Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results
summary: Revenue Increases 9.4% and Net Income Rises 25.5% Year-over-Year; Earnings Per Share Reaches $0.50...
body_text: CHENGDU, China, Aug. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- WeTouch Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: WETH) (“WeTouch” or the “Company”), a global provider of touch display solutions, today announced its unaudited financial results for the first half of fiscal year 2026 ended June 30, 2026. Revenue growth was supported by continued expansion across the Company’s core markets, while its overseas business maintained positive momentum as the Company continued to develop new markets and channels. First Half Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Highlights Total Revenue: $30.3 million, an increase of 9.4% from $27.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Gross Profit: $10.7 million, up 9.8% from $9.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Gross Margin: 35.3%, compared with 35.2% in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Income from Operations: $8.3 million, up 16.9% from $7.1 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Net Income: $6.0 million, up 25.5% from $4.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Basic and Diluted Earnings Per Share: $0.50, compared with $0.40 in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Operating Cash Flow: $5.5 million, compared with $4.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Cash Reserves: $127.5 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with $110.5 million as of June 30, 2025. Overseas Revenue: $9.7 million, an increase of 7.8% from $9.0 million in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Total Volume Shipped: approximately 1.43 million units, an increase of 3.5% from approximately 1.38 million units in the first half of fiscal year 2025. Stockholders’ Equity: $148.8 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with $131.8 million as of June 30, 2025. Management Commentary “WeTouch delivered solid growth in the first half of fiscal year 2026, with revenue increasing 9.4% and net income increasing 25.5% year-over-year,” said Zongyi Lian, Chief Executive Officer of WeTouch Technology Inc. “The results reflect steady demand across our core end markets, disciplined cost management and continued operating efficiency. We achieved growth across all major product categories, led by automotive and medical touchscreen applications. Our overseas business also maintained positive momentum, supported by continued investment in new market channels and customer development. Recent business initiatives in Japan and Singapore further demonstrate the Company’s progress in expanding its international market coverage.” “Looking ahead, WeTouch will continue to build on its core touch display capabilities and advance from a component supplier toward a provider of integrated touch display modules and professional solutions, while exploring opportunities in intelligent hardware, robotics and AI-enabled terminals.” Mr. Lian continued, “The recently announced special cash dividend represents an initial step toward developing a more balanced capital allocation and stockholder return framework. We recognize the importance of balancing shareholder returns with continued investment in growth opportunities. Going forward, our Board and management will continue to evaluate appropriate ways to enhance shareholder value, which may include potential dividends, share repurchases and other capital return measures, taking into account the Company’s cash position, operating needs, growth strategy, market conditions and applicable legal and regulatory requirements. In addition, the proposed strategic investment by entities affiliated with our management and controlling shareholder, which remains subject to shareholder approval and other customary closing conditions, is intended to strengthen WeTouch’s capital base and support the Company’s long-term strategic development. We believe the proposed investment and related lock-up arrangements reflect management’s confidence in the Company’s future and further align management’s interests with those of shareholders. We also recognize the importance of transparent communication with shareholders and encourage shareholders to review the Company’s proxy materials carefully before making their voting decision.” Business and Strategic Outlook Core Business Growth: Continue strengthening the Company’s position in automotive, industrial control, point-of-sale, gaming, medical and other specialized touchscreen applications. Overseas Market Expansion: Continue investing in regional channels, customer development and project-based cooperation in Asia and other international markets, including ongoing initiatives involving Japan and Singapore. Solutions and Integration: Further develop touch display modules, customized solutions and system-integration capabilities to increase value delivered to customers. Intelligent Hardware Opportunities: Explore applications in intelligent terminals, robotics and other AI-enabled hardware that can leverage the Company’s touch display, human-machine interaction and manufacturing capabilities. About WeTouch Technology Inc. WeTouch Technology Inc. is a global provider of medium- to large-sized projected capacitive touchscreens and touch display solutions. The Company’s products are used in a broad range of applications, including automotive, industrial control, point-of-sale terminals, gaming and lottery equipment, medical devices, multi-functional printers and other specialized human-machine-interface applications. WeTouch is committed to expanding from core touch display components toward integrated modules, professional solutions and intelligent hardware applications. For additional information, please visit the Company’s website at http://en.usa-wetouch.com/. Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements include, among other things, statements regarding the Company’s business strategy, overseas market expansion, channel development, product and solution development, intelligent hardware opportunities, future growth and operating plans. These statements are based on management’s current expectations and assumptions and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements. Additional information regarding these and other risks and uncertainties is included in the Company’s filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which are available at www.sec.gov. title: 10 Best Quote and Proposal Software Platforms for 2026 (Buyer's Guide)
summary: he 10 best quote and proposal software platforms for 2026, compared. Features, pricing, ideal buyer, and a decision framework for sales teams, agencies, and professional services firms.
body_text: Quote and proposal software is where deal velocity now lives. The average B2B buyer expects a personalized, e-signable, price-configured proposal delivered within hours of a discovery call not days. Teams that still send static Word documents attached to email lose deals to teams that send interactive proposals with live pricing, embedded video, and one-click signature. The proposal-software market is projected to grow at roughly 11% CAGR through 2030 , according to industry analyst reports ( Gartner CPQ Software market reviews ), driven by AI-generated content, deeper CPQ integrations, and collapse of boundary between proposal, contract, and e-signature. That growth has produced a crowded market dozens of platforms, overlapping feature sets, and pricing that ranges from $19/user/month at low end to enterprise contracts north of $100,000/year. This guide covers ten platforms that consistently rank at top of buyer shortlists in 2026, how they differ, who each is best for, and a decision framework at end for narrowing down. It is written for sales, revenue-ops, professional-services firm , and agency buyers who actually have to pick one. What is quote and proposal software Quote and proposal software is a category of sales-enablement platform that lets teams create, send, track, and close business proposals including quotes, statements of work, engagement letters, and contracts from a single interface. It replaces older workflow of drafting proposals in Word, converting to PDF, emailing an attachment, and chasing signatures manually. The category overlaps with CPQ (Configure-Price-Quote) at enterprise end and with contract lifecycle management (CLM) at post-signature end, but core value delivered by every tool in this list is same: shorten time between "we'd like to see a proposal" and a signed agreement. Key features to look for Templates and content library. Reusable blocks pricing tables, scope-of-work sections, case studies so reps do not rewrite same proposal twice. Configure-Price-Quote (CPQ). Rule-based product configuration, discount approvals, and quote pricing that matches your actual price book. E-signature. Legally-binding signature capture, ideally without a separate DocuSign contract. Real-time tracking and analytics. Notification when prospect opens proposal, which section they spend time in, and whether they forwarded it internally. CRM integration. Bidirectional sync with Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive so quote data flows both ways without duplicate entry. Interactive elements. Embedded video, live pricing widgets, ROI calculators proposals that behave more like landing pages than PDFs. Payment collection. Take a deposit or first invoice at moment of signature, especially important for Client Accounting Services firms and agencies on retainer who then sync those invoices back into QuickBooks or Xero. Benefits for business Teams using proposal software typically see 30–40% faster proposal turnaround , higher close rates on shorter cycles, and materially better visibility into where deals stall. For services firms sending recurring engagement letters where pricing tiers and scope are updated annually recurring-proposal automation alone often pays for tool. Firms that pair proposal automation with clean monthly reconciliation recover margin end-to-end rather than losing it to manual bookkeeping downstream. How we evaluated platforms The ten platforms below were selected on four dimensions: (1) breadth of features across templates, CPQ, e-sign, and analytics; (2) integration ecosystem, especially CRM and payment; (3) pricing transparency and value at small-to-mid segment; (4) verified user review volume on G2's proposal software category and Capterra with a 4.0+ average. Enterprise-only platforms with custom-quoted pricing appear where they are meaningfully dominant in their segment. AI-generation features were considered but not required every platform in this list now offers some form of AI drafting. Quote and proposal software comparison Platform Best for Starting price CPQ E-sign Free trial PandaDoc End-to-end document workflows $35/user/mo Yes Yes 14-day Proposify Design-first agencies $49/user/mo Yes Yes 14-day Better Proposals Small agencies and consultants $19/user/mo Limited Yes 14-day Qwilr Modern interactive web proposals $35/user/mo Yes Yes 14-day GetAccept Sales teams with heavy CRM use $49/user/mo Yes Yes 14-day Oneflow Contract-first, dynamic documents Free (limited); paid from $19/user/mo Yes Yes Yes DealHub Revenue operations and sales-ops Custom Full CPQ Yes Demo only QuoteWerks SMB, MSPs, resellers, distributors ~$199/user/mo (perpetual + subscription) Full CPQ Yes 30-day Salesforce Revenue Cloud Enterprise Salesforce shops Custom (from ~$75/user/mo) Full CPQ Yes Demo only Conga CPQ Enterprise with complex configuration Custom Full CPQ Yes Demo only ‍ Pricing is listed at published starting tiers as of early 2026 and does not include implementation or add-on modules enterprise buyers should expect meaningful uplift over sticker. The 10 best quote and proposal software in 2026 1. PandaDoc Best for: Sales, revenue ops, and services teams that want a single platform for proposals, contracts, and e-signature without stitching three vendors together. PandaDoc is most broadly deployed platform in category and shows up on nearly every buyer shortlist for a reason it does templates, content library, CPQ, e-signature, payments, and analytics in one interface, and its Salesforce and HubSpot integrations are among most mature in market. The template library is deep enough that most teams do not need to build from scratch on day one. Recent releases have leaned heavily into AI proposal drafting from a discovery-call transcript or from CRM opportunity data. Payment collection at signature is native (Stripe integration), which matters for agencies and CAS firms that want deposits on spot. Where PandaDoc gets criticism: pricing tiers gate a lot of good features (approval workflows, advanced analytics, unlimited templates), and mid-tier plan is where most teams end up rather than entry plan. Occasional PDF rendering quirks on complex layouts. Pricing: $35/user/mo Essentials, $65 Business, custom Enterprise · Free trial: 14 days. 2. Proposify Best for: Agencies, consultancies, and creative shops where proposal itself is a design artifact and needs to look every bit as good as client's brand guidelines. Proposify was built by an agency and it shows. The editor is closer to a design tool than a document editor precise control over typography, spacing, and image placement and template library is stronger on visual polish than on operational scale. For agencies that pitch on positioning and creative, Proposify frequently wins over PandaDoc for exactly that reason. Content library, CPQ (called "Pricing tables"), e-signature, and CRM integrations are all present. Analytics are more focused on section-level engagement than on cross-team pipeline reporting. Where Proposify is weaker: less depth on complex enterprise CPQ (multi-tier discount workflows, product bundling), and pricing has crept up in recent years, making it noticeably more expensive than Better Proposals for similar-size teams. Pricing: $49/user/mo Team, $65 Business · Free trial: 14 days. 3. Better Proposals Best for: Small agencies, freelancers, and consultants who want a low-friction proposal tool that is affordable and fast to learn. Better Proposals is cost-effective option in category and is platform most new-to-proposal-software teams start with. The template library is large, editor is straightforward, and pricing tier is among lowest of any serious proposal tool at $19/user/mo. E-sign, live-chat inside proposal, and payment collection are included on lower tiers than at competitors. Where Better Proposals gets thinner: CPQ is basic (fine for simple retainers or one-line-item pricing, less capable for multi-tier configuration), analytics are lighter than PandaDoc or GetAccept, and integrations are shallower than enterprise-oriented tools. For a two-to-ten-person agency, Better Proposals is often right answer for years before outgrowing it. Pricing: $19/user/mo Starter, $29 Premium, $49 Enterprise · Free trial: 14 days. 4. Qwilr Best for: Modern sales teams that want their proposals to feel like interactive web pages, not documents. Qwilr's differentiator is format. Proposals are rendered as responsive web pages embedded video, live pricing widgets, ROI calculators, interactive tables buyer can toggle rather than PDF-style documents. For technology, SaaS, and services companies selling to buyers who expect a modern digital experience, Qwilr materially raises perceived polish. CPQ is capable (rule-based pricing, tiered options), e-sign is native, and analytics show which sections of page buyer spent time on. Salesforce and HubSpot integrations are solid. The trade-off: some buyers still want a PDF they can print or email internally, and Qwilr's PDF export is functional but not always as clean as interactive version. For heavily-regulated industries (financial services, healthcare) some legal teams still push back on non-document proposals. Pricing: $35/user/mo Business, $59 Enterprise · Free trial: 14 days. 5. GetAccept Best for: Sales teams whose revenue-ops workflow lives inside Salesforce or HubSpot and who want proposal-to-signature velocity as their primary metric. GetAccept is CRM-native option in category. The Salesforce and HubSpot integrations are among deepest available quote data, opportunity stages, and buyer-engagement signals flow both ways and platform treats "digital sales rooms" as a first-class concept, meaning proposals live inside a shared buyer-and-seller workspace rather than as static documents. Features cover CPQ, e-signature, video personalization, and live chat inside proposal. Analytics on buyer engagement are among strongest in category, which is what CRM-heavy teams tend to care about most. Weaker areas: pricing sits at higher end of mid-market, and platform is less compelling for teams that are not already deep in Salesforce or HubSpot. Pricing: $49/user/mo Essentials, custom higher tiers · Free trial: 14 days. 6. Oneflow Best for: Teams that want contract lifecycle management folded into proposal dynamic documents editable in real time after send. Oneflow's unique angle is "dynamic contract." A proposal sent through Oneflow can be edited by either party after send counterparty can propose changes inline, negotiations happen in document itself, and final signed version is generated from current state rather than a PDF re-send. That workflow is meaningfully different from every other tool on this list. Contract lifecycle features (post-signature amendments, renewals, storage) are stronger than at pure proposal tools. Integrations to Salesforce, HubSpot, and other CRMs are solid, and pricing tier is one of more approachable in category including a free tier that is genuinely usable for small teams. Where Oneflow is thinner: "dynamic contract" model is powerful but new to many buyers and takes some internal education. Some CPQ workflows are less mature than at DealHub or Conga. Pricing: Free (limited); paid from $19/user/mo Essentials, custom Business/Enterprise · Free trial: Yes. 7. DealHub Best for: Revenue-ops teams that need full CPQ, deal desk, and contract management as one integrated stack. DealHub is where category shades into full CPQ. It handles product configuration, pricing rules, discount approvals, deal desk workflows, contract management, and e-signature all with heavy Salesforce native integration. Teams selecting DealHub typically have complex pricing (usage-based, tiered, bundled) that lighter tools cannot model cleanly. Reporting and analytics on deal velocity, discount leakage, and quote-to-cash cycle time are enterprise-grade. The trade-off is complexity: DealHub is not a tool a two-person sales team should buy, and implementation typically runs 6–12 weeks with a professional-services engagement. Pricing is entirely custom, and buyers should expect DealHub to sit at higher end of platform stack cost. Pricing: Custom (typically $50K+ ARR) · Free trial: Demo only. 8. QuoteWerks Best for: SMB technology resellers, MSPs, IT distributors, and value-added resellers who need product-catalog-driven quoting. QuoteWerks has been in category for longer than most tools on this list and dominates IT reseller and MSP segment specifically. Its integrations with distributor catalogs (Ingram Micro, Tech Data, D&H) mean a rep can pull live pricing and availability into a quote without leaving tool a workflow no other proposal tool replicates as cleanly. CRM integrations, e-signature, and CPQ are all present, and platform runs both on-premises and in cloud, which some IT resellers still prefer for data-residency reasons. Interface is more utilitarian than Qwilr or Proposify this is a tool for operators, not designers. Best fit: teams selling hardware, software licenses, or bundled IT services where product catalog volume matters more than proposal aesthetics. Pricing: ~$199/user/mo (perpetual + subscription hybrid); volume discounts · Free trial: 30 days. 9. Salesforce Revenue Cloud Best for: Enterprise Salesforce shops that want CPQ, billing, and revenue management as a native Salesforce application. Salesforce Revenue Cloud (which absorbed former Salesforce CPQ product) is incumbent enterprise choice for organizations already committed to Salesforce platform. Native integration is total quote objects, price books, opportunity data, and forecasts share one data model and platform scales to genuinely large product catalogs and multi-tier discount structures. E-signature is available through Salesforce Sign or integration to DocuSign. AI-assisted quote generation and revenue forecasting have expanded significantly with Einstein platform. The trade-off: implementation is complex, per-user costs are among highest in category, and non-Salesforce customers see essentially no reason to pick it over PandaDoc or DealHub. This is a decision made by Salesforce shops, not by tools shopping category cold. Pricing: Custom, typically from ~$75/user/mo for CPQ · Free trial: Demo only. 10. Conga CPQ Best for: Large enterprises with complex product configuration, multi-entity pricing, and heavy compliance requirements. Conga is other enterprise CPQ heavyweight alongside Salesforce Revenue Cloud. It handles same problem set complex product configuration, guided selling, deal desk, contract management with strong support for manufacturing, life sciences, and financial services verticals. Its document generation (Conga Composer) is a category unto itself for template-based document assembly at scale. Where Conga wins over Salesforce Revenue Cloud: platform-agnostic CRM support (works with Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, and others equally well) and stronger document assembly features. Where it loses: it does not have native tightness of a same-vendor stack that Revenue Cloud gets inside Salesforce. Pricing: Custom · Free trial: Demo only. Key features to weigh in your decision Every platform in this list handles core "send a proposal and collect a signature" workflow. The differentiators sit in five areas: CPQ depth. Rule-based product configuration, discount approval workflows, and price-book integration are where enterprise tools separate from mid-market tools. If your product catalog has more than 200 SKUs or your pricing has multiple discount tiers, mid-market tools will hit their limits. CRM integration depth. "Integrates with Salesforce" spans a wide range. GetAccept, DealHub, and Salesforce Revenue Cloud have deep bidirectional sync; some others are effectively one-way at quote-created event. Design flexibility. Agency and services buyers weight this heavily; enterprise CPQ buyers rarely do. Contract lifecycle features. If you need to manage renewals, amendments, and post-signature revisions, Oneflow, DealHub, and Conga are stronger than pure proposal tools. Payment capture at signature. Native Stripe or ACH support at signature is a meaningful workflow reduction for services firms that use QuickBooks for invoicing and want deposits collected upfront. How to choose right platform The right tool depends on team size, deal complexity, existing tech stack, and how much design polish proposal itself needs to carry. Five questions to run through before shortlisting: 1. How complex is your pricing? If pricing is a single line item or a tiered retainer, any of mid-market tools will do. If you have multi-tier discounting, product bundles, and approval workflows, only CPQ-heavy platforms (DealHub, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Conga) will not hit walls. 2. Where does your CRM live? Salesforce shops with big Salesforce spend should evaluate Revenue Cloud first. HubSpot shops should look at PandaDoc, GetAccept, and Proposify. Non-CRM teams have wider optionality. 3. Who at your company actually opens proposal? If answer is "a designer or a marketer approves layout before send," Proposify or Qwilr are worth premium. If answer is "rep sends what CRM generates," design flexibility matters less. 4. Do you need post-signature workflow? Renewals, amendments, quote-to-cash automation, and contract storage. If yes, Oneflow, DealHub, or Conga are stronger picks than pure proposal tools. 5. What is realistic budget per user per month? For a two-to-ten-person team, budget $19–$65 per user. For mid-market (10–50 users) plan on $35–$100 per user with negotiation on enterprise tier. For 50+ users with complex CPQ, expect custom pricing that starts around $75/user/mo and rises with implementation. The wrong reason to pick a tool is because a specific competitor uses it. The right reason is that tool handles your top three workflow bottlenecks better than alternatives. Where proposal software fits with accounting automation For professional services firms agencies, consultancies, and accounting practices sending recurring engagement letters proposal software solves upstream half of revenue workflow. The downstream half is what happens once proposal is signed: invoicing, revenue recognition, reconciliation , and month-end close. Firms that automate both sides recover meaningful hours per client per month. That downstream automation is what Finlens handles categorization, close, and multi-client reconciliation across an entire book of business so same firm that just signed a new client via PandaDoc or Proposify does not lose margin on manual bookkeeping afterward. Conclusion The right quote and proposal software depends on your deal complexity, your CRM stack, and how much your proposal design needs to carry sale. For most mid-market teams, PandaDoc, Proposify, Qwilr, and GetAccept form shortlist worth demoing. Small agencies do well with Better Proposals. Enterprise teams with heavy CPQ requirements land at DealHub, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, or Conga. Services firms wanting integrated contract lifecycle should evaluate Oneflow. IT resellers and MSPs remain best-served by QuoteWerks. Book a 20-minute walkthrough with Finlens if you run a professional-services or accounting practice proposal software solves top half of your revenue workflow, and Finlens solves accounting-close half that determines whether margin on those signed proposals actually reaches P&L. FAQ What is difference between proposal software and CPQ software? Proposal software is broader it covers document creation, e-signature, and buyer engagement. CPQ (Configure-Price-Quote) is a subset focused on rule-based product configuration and pricing. Enterprise tools like DealHub, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, and Conga combine both. Mid-market tools like PandaDoc, Proposify, and Better Proposals offer lighter CPQ inside a broader proposal platform. Can proposal software collect payment at signature? Yes. PandaDoc, Proposify, Better Proposals, and GetAccept all support payment collection at signature through Stripe or similar processors. This is especially valuable for services firms wanting deposits or first-month retainers on spot. How much does quote and proposal software cost? Entry pricing starts at ~$19/user/mo (Better Proposals) and rises to $35–$65/user/mo for mid-market (PandaDoc, Proposify, Qwilr, GetAccept). Enterprise CPQ (DealHub, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Conga) is custom and typically starts around $75/user/mo with meaningful implementation costs on top. Is proposal software worth it for a small team? Yes for any team sending more than 5–10 proposals per month. Even at entry tier of ~$19–$35/user/mo, time saved on template reuse, e-signature, and follow-up tracking pays back tool within first month for most teams. What is ROI timeline for implementing proposal software? Most teams report proposal-turnaround time drops 30–40% in first 60 days, with measurable close-rate improvements in first 90 days. Total-cost payback typically lands under 90 days at mid-market tiers, longer for enterprise CPQ where implementation itself takes months.

body_text: Three XPO Drivers Earn Top Awards at 2026 National Truck Driving Championships August 18, 2026 PDF Version GREENWICH, Conn., Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPO (NYSE: XPO ), a leading provider of freight transportation in North America, today announced that three of its drivers earned top honors at the 2026 National Truck Driving Championships ( NTDC ). Chris Poynor of Pasco, Washington, placed first in the 3-Axle class. An accomplished competitor, Chris was named Grand Champion of the 2026 Washington Truck Driving Championships and previously won two national titles in the Twins class. He has driven more than two million consecutive accident-free miles over his 27-year career with XPO. Two other XPO drivers earned spots on the podium at this year’s national championships: Dave May (Buffalo, New York): Placed second in the Straight Truck class. A U.S. Army veteran, Dave made his 15th appearance at nationals and has served as a captain on America’s Road Team. Jeff Halford (Boise, Idaho): Placed third in the 3-Axle class. Jeff has driven for XPO for more than 30 years and returned to nationals for the 14th time. He has also served as a captain on America’s Road Team. Mario Harik, chairman and chief executive officer of XPO, said, “Congratulations to Chris, Dave and Jeff for their outstanding performances at NTDC. We’re proud of them and of all 36 XPO drivers who competed at nationals this year. Their skill, professionalism and commitment to safety represent the best of our industry.” 36 XPO drivers from 23 states competed in the 2026 NTDC, hosted by the American Trucking Associations (ATA) in Pittsburgh from August 11-14. Each driver qualified by winning one of nine vehicle classes at their state truck driving championships and maintaining an accident-free driving record for at least one year prior to the competition. A complete overview of XPO’s national qualifiers can be found at https://bit.ly/XPO-NTDC26 . About XPO XPO, Inc. (NYSE: XPO) is a leader in asset-based less-than-truckload (LTL) freight transportation in North America. The company’s customer-focused organization efficiently moves 16 billion pounds of freight per year, enabled by its proprietary technology. XPO serves 55,000 customers with 586 locations and 38,000 employees in North America and Europe, and is headquartered in Greenwich, Conn., USA.
