The 10 Best RevOps Tools & Platforms in 2026
summary: Build a smarter RevOps stack with our guide to 10 leading tools for CRM, forecasting, data enrichment, lead routing, compensation and sales execution.
body_text: Revenue operations has graduated from a back office alignment function to the strategic engine behind predictable growth — and the software stack has grown up with it . If you are evaluating the best RevOps tools for 2026, the short answer is that no single platform does everything: the strongest stacks pair a system of record (HubSpot or Salesforce) with a revenue intelligence layer (Clari, Gong), a data foundation (ZoomInfo, Clearbit), routing and orchestration (LeanData, Default), compensation (QuotaPath), and an execution layer that moves conversations forward (Trellus). Below, we review ten leading revenue operations platforms and tools, what each is best for, their standout features, and an honest limitation — so you can assemble a stack that fits how your team sells. Revenue operations exists to unify sales, marketing, and customer success around one shared view of the pipeline. According to Gartner's research on revenue operations , organizations that consolidate these functions under a single RevOps model see stronger forecast accuracy and tighter go to market alignment. That's the lens we used to build this list: how well each tool contributes to a connected, measurable revenue engine. How We Chose the Best RevOps Tools Before the list, a quick word on evaluation. The RevOps category spans several distinct jobs — customer data unification, revenue intelligence and forecasting, sales pipeline orchestration, and sales and marketing automation. A tool that dominates one job may be irrelevant to another, so "best" always depends on the gap you're filling. We weighted these criteria: • Category fit — does it own a clear job (forecasting, data, routing, execution) or try to do everything at a lower scale? • Integration depth — RevOps lives on clean data flowing between systems, so native CRM and SEP connections matter more than feature count. • Time to value — how fast a lean RevOps team can deploy it without a six month implementation. • Data quality and governance — the foundation everything downstream depends on. • Price transparency and scalability — whether the tool grows with headcount and deal volume without punishing surprises. The 10 Best RevOps Tools & Platforms in 2026 RevOps Tool Category Best For Standout Feature Key Limitation HubSpot CRM & GTM Platform Mid-market & scaling teams Unified customer record & workflow automation Costs can rise quickly as teams scale Clari Revenue Intelligence Forecast-focused RevOps teams AI forecasting & pipeline inspection Enterprise pricing & implementation overhead Gong Conversation Intelligence Sales coaching & forecast insight Call analysis & deal intelligence Premium pricing; limited direct execution Trellus Sales Execution & Coaching High-volume outbound teams Embedded parallel dialer & real-time AI coaching Requires separate CRM & data provider ZoomInfo B2B Data & Intelligence Data-driven GTM teams Contact data, intent & enrichment Expensive with ongoing data verification needs QuotaPath Compensation Management RevOps & finance teams Real-time earnings & comp tracking Complex enterprise plans need configuration Salesforce Revenue Cloud Revenue Lifecycle Management Salesforce enterprises Quote-to-cash & complex revenue workflows Complex implementation & higher cost Default Inbound Revenue Orchestration Inbound & product-led teams Lead routing, enrichment & scheduling Younger ecosystem; inbound focused Clearbit Data Enrichment Marketing & RevOps teams Real-time enrichment & visitor identification Increasingly tied to the HubSpot ecosystem LeanData Lead Routing & Orchestration Salesforce-based teams Lead-to-account matching & routing logic Salesforce-centric and built for scale 1. HubSpot What it is: An all in one CRM and go to market platform spanning marketing, sales, service, and operations hubs. For many mid market RevOps teams, HubSpot is the system of record that everything else plugs into. Best for: Mid market and scaling companies that want one connected platform for sales and marketing automation rather than stitching point solutions together. Standout features: A genuinely unified customer record across marketing and sales, strong workflow automation, a deep app marketplace, and Operations Hub for data sync, deduplication, and programmable automations — a real asset for customer data unification. Limitation: Costs escalate quickly as you add hubs, seats, and marketing contacts, and its native forecasting and revenue intelligence are lighter than dedicated tools like Clari. Larger enterprises with complex CPQ needs often outgrow it. 2. Clari What it is: A revenue platform built around forecasting and pipeline management. Clari ingests activity data across your stack to give leaders a real time, AI driven view of where the number will land. Best for: Sales and RevOps leaders who live and die by forecast accuracy and want to run disciplined, defensible forecast calls. Standout features: AI based projected forecasting, pipeline inspection that flags at-risk deals, and "RevDB" — a warehouse grade data model unifying signals from CRM, email, calendar, and conversations. Its acquisition of Groove also gives it a sales engagement footprint. Limitation: It's an enterprise priced platform with real implementation overhead; smaller teams may find it heavy, and its value is proportional to how disciplined your CRM hygiene already is. 3. Gong What it is: A revenue intelligence platform anchored in conversation data. Gong captures and analyzes calls, emails, and meetings to surface what's being said in deals — a category leader in revenue intelligence and forecasting. Best for: Teams that want to coach at scale and pressure test the forecast with hard conversation evidence rather than rep optimism. Standout features: Automatic call recording and transcription, deal and pipeline warnings driven by real interactions, market intelligence on competitor mentions and topics, and increasingly strong forecasting built on that signal base. Limitation: It's premium priced and shines mostly once you have call volume to analyze. As a system of insight rather than execution, Gong tells you what's happening but doesn't place the next call for you — you still need an execution layer for that. 4. Trellus What it is: Trellus is the outbound calling and conversation execution layer of a modern RevOps stack . It's an AI powered sales acceleration and coaching platform whose signature product is an embedded parallel dialer that runs inside the tools reps already use — Salesloft, Outreach, Apollo, HubSpot, and Salesforce — through a Chrome extension, so reps never context-switch into a separate dialer app. Where Clari and Gong tell RevOps what's happening in the pipeline, Trellus is where reps actually generate the connected conversations that fill it. Best for: SDR/BDR and AE teams running high volume outbound calling who want to multiply live connects without leaving their existing sales engagement platforms for RevOps teams. It's also a strong fit for remote and hybrid teams that need live coaching and visibility. Standout features: • Parallel dialer that dials up to ~5 lines simultaneously to multiply connect rates, with automated voicemail drop and automatic call logging back to your SEP/CRM. • Real time AI coaching delivered on screen mid call — objection handling, competitor battle cards, and customizable talk tracks — plus AI voice agents that double as 24/7 practice partners. • Call analytics that score 100% of calls (not samples), surfacing the behavior gaps between top and bottom performers, viewable in a shared Virtual Sales Floor for live coaching and call blitzes. Because it captures every call as structured activity, Trellus feeds clean execution data straight into the revenue intelligence and forecasting layer — supporting broader sales automation goals and stronger SDR efficiency across the team. Pricing is aggressive and self-serve: ‍ Power and Parallel plans run $99.99/mo and $149.99 per mo (with a custom priced Business tier adding team analytics and AI modeling. Limitation: Trellus is a calling and conversation execution layer, not a full CRM or a B2B contact database — you pair it with your data provider and CRM rather than replacing them. Parallel dialing also rewards good list hygiene and TCPA/DNC discipline, and it's a younger brand than incumbents like Salesloft. For RevOps leaders assembling intelligent sales automation tools, that focus is a feature: it does execution exceptionally well and stays in its lane. 5. ZoomInfo What it is: A go to market intelligence platform combining a large B2B contact and company database with intent signals and workflow tools. For many RevOps teams, ZoomInfo is the data foundation the rest of the stack enriches against. Best for: Teams that need accurate firmographic and contact data plus buyer intent signals to prioritize accounts and power outbound. Standout features: Deep B2B contact and company data, intent and scoops signals, and native enrichment plus routing via ZoomInfo OperationsOS to keep CRM records current — a serious asset for customer data unification and account intelligence that supports better sales prospecting tools workflows. Limitation: It's one of the pricier data platforms, contracts can be rigid, and data accuracy — while strong — still requires ongoing verification, especially for direct dial mobile numbers. 6. QuotaPath What it is: A commission and compensation management platform that automates how variable pay is calculated, tracked, and paid — an often overlooked but core piece of the RevOps stack. Best for: RevOps and finance teams tired of running comp in error prone spreadsheets who want reps to see earnings in real time. Standout features: Flexible comp plan builder, real time earnings visibility for reps, CRM and payroll integrations, and quota attainment reporting that ties compensation directly to pipeline data. Limitation: It's purpose built for compensation, so it's a complement rather than a hub — and very complex, multi tiered enterprise plans can still require careful configuration or a heavier tool like CaptivateIQ. 7. Salesforce Revenue Cloud What it is: Salesforce's suite for revenue lifecycle management — CPQ, billing, subscription management, and contract handling — built on the world's most widely deployed CRM platform. Best for: Enterprises already standardized on Salesforce that need configure price quote, billing, and complex revenue workflows unified with the CRM. Standout features: End to end quote to cash, deep configurability, native tie in to the broader Salesforce ecosystem (including Agentforce and Data Cloud), and enterprise grade governance for sales pipeline orchestration at scale. Limitation: Power comes with complexity and cost — implementations typically require admins or partners, and time to value is measured in months, not days. It's overkill for smaller teams whose needs a lighter CPQ tool would meet. 8. Default.com What it is: A newer inbound revenue orchestration platform that unifies lead capture, enrichment, qualification, routing, and scheduling into a single automated workflow — collapsing the "speed to lead" stack into one tool. Best for: Product led and inbound heavy teams that want to convert form fills into booked meetings instantly, without duct taping five point solutions together. Standout features: Instant lead routing and scheduling, built in enrichment, form and workflow builders, and a modern approach to pipeline orchestration that competes with LeanData on speed and simplicity. Limitation: As a younger entrant, its ecosystem and integrations are still maturing versus incumbents, and it's most valuable for inbound motions — outbound first teams will lean on other tools in this list. 9. Clearbit What it is: A B2B data enrichment and intelligence tool (now part of HubSpot, offered as Breeze Intelligence) that enriches records with firmographic and technographic data in real time and reveals anonymous website visitors. Best for: Marketing and RevOps teams that want to enrich inbound leads, shorten forms, and unify customer data automatically on the way into the CRM. Standout features: Real time enrichment APIs, website visitor de anonymization for account based plays, and tight native integration with HubSpot for automated data unification and scoring. Limitation: Since the HubSpot acquisition, standalone flexibility has narrowed, and it's increasingly positioned within the HubSpot ecosystem — less ideal if your system of record is Salesforce or you want a neutral, best of breed data layer. 10. LeanData What it is: The category-defining lead-to-account matching and revenue orchestration platform. LeanData ensures every lead, contact, and account is matched, routed, and assigned to the right owner automatically. Best for: Salesforce based teams with complex routing rules, account based motions, or large SDR/AE teams where fair, fast lead distribution directly affects pipeline. Standout features: A visual flowbuilder for routing logic, robust lead to account matching, round robin and territory assignment, and orchestration that ties marketing and sales handoffs together — foundational sales pipeline orchestration. Limitation: It's tightly coupled to Salesforce and priced for scale, so it's less relevant for HubSpot native or very small teams. Sophisticated routing trees also demand ongoing RevOps ownership to maintain. How to Build the Right RevOps Stack The tools above solve different problems, so the goal isn't to buy the most — it's to cover each layer once, cleanly. A practical framework: • System of record: Start with HubSpot or Salesforce as the single source of truth. Everything else should read from and write to it. • Data foundation: Layer in ZoomInfo or Clearbit so your records stay enriched and deduplicated. Dirty data undermines every downstream forecast and automation. • Orchestration: Add LeanData or Default so leads route to the right rep in seconds — speed to lead is one of the highest ROI fixes in RevOps. • Revenue intelligence and forecasting: Bring in Clari for forecast discipline and Gong for conversation-level insight so leadership steers with evidence, not gut feel. • Execution: Give reps an execution layer like Trellus so the pipeline your data and orchestration create actually turns into live conversations — reinforcing your outbound sales strategy rather than just measuring it. • Compensation: Close the loop with QuotaPath, so incentives map cleanly to the behaviors your data shows drive revenue. The discipline is integration over accumulation. Forrester's research on revenue operations and B2B growth consistently ties predictable revenue to aligned processes and shared data across the funnel — a point reinforced across Forrester's B2B and RevOps coverage. Overlapping tools that don't talk to each other create the exact data silos RevOps was invented to eliminate. When you evaluate any addition, ask whether it deepens the connected system or just adds another dashboard. Strong best AI sales platforms increasingly bake this integration in, which is why native connectivity should outrank raw feature count on your shortlist. Getting the stack right also has a direct financial payoff: fewer redundant tools, less manual reconciliation, and faster conversion all help lower customer acquisition cost — often the metric that justifies the RevOps investment to your CFO. Frequently Asked Questions What are RevOps tools? RevOps tools are software platforms that unify revenue operations across sales , marketing, and customer success. They span CRM systems of record, data enrichment, lead routing and orchestration, revenue intelligence and forecasting, compensation, and execution layers like dialers — all working from one shared view of the pipeline so revenue becomes predictable and measurable. Do I need a dedicated RevOps platform or a stack of tools? For most teams, a stack. No single platform excels at CRM, data, forecasting, routing, compensation, and execution simultaneously. The best RevOps tools each own a clear job and integrate tightly. Start with a strong system of record, then add best of breed layers as gaps appear rather than forcing one tool to do everything shallowly. What's the difference between revenue intelligence and revenue operations? Revenue operations is the broader function — aligning people, process, and data across the go to market motion. Revenue intelligence is one capability within it: using AI to analyze deals, conversations, and activity to improve forecasting and coaching. Tools like Clari and Gong deliver revenue intelligence; the RevOps stack surrounding them handles data, routing, and execution. Where does an outbound dialer fit in a RevOps stack? It's the execution layer. Data tools find the right accounts and forecasting tools tell you where the number will land, but reps still have to have conversations. An embedded parallel dialer like Trellus multiplies live connects and auto logs every call as structured activity, feeding clean execution data back into the revenue intelligence and forecasting systems. See our guide to the best sales prospecting tools for how the data and execution layers connect. Which RevOps tool is best for a small or mid market team? HubSpot is usually the best starting hub for mid market teams thanks to its all in one design and faster time to value. From there, add a data layer (Clearbit or ZoomInfo) and an execution layer (Trellus) before investing in enterprise grade forecasting. Larger, Salesforce based orgs will lean toward Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Clari, and LeanData. The Bottom Line The best RevOps tools in 2026 aren't a single winner — they're a well integrated stack where each layer does one job exceptionally well and shares clean data with the rest. Anchor on a system of record, enforce data quality, orchestrate your leads, forecast with evidence, and — critically — give reps a real execution layer so all that infrastructure converts into conversations. That last layer is where Trellus earns its place: an embedded parallel dialer with real time AI coaching that multiplies connects and logs every call back into your revenue engine, without pulling reps out of the tools they already use.

title: Mounjaro and Wegovy Safety Concerns Grow as UK Records Thousands of Suspected Side Effects

body_text: Weight loss injections have become one of the biggest developments in modern obesity treatment, offering new hope for people struggling with weight management. Medicines such as Mounjaro and Wegovy have gained widespread attention because of their ability to reduce appetite, support weight loss, and improve certain health outcomes when used correctly. However, new safety reports have raised concerns among patients and healthcare professionals after thousands of suspected side effect reports involving weight loss medications were recorded in the UK. Data from the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) shows that reports of adverse reactions, including serious cases and deaths, have been submitted for drugs including tirzepatide, semaglutide, and liraglutide. It is important to understand that these reports do not prove that the medicines directly caused every reported illness or death. Safety reports are investigated carefully, and many factors, including existing health conditions, can influence outcomes. Thousands of Adverse Reaction Reports Linked to Weight Loss Medicines According to MHRA Yellow Card reporting data, thousands of suspected adverse reactions have been reported among people using weight loss injections available in the UK. The medicines involved include: Tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro Semaglutide, the active ingredient in Wegovy Liraglutide, used in medicines such as Saxenda The reports include both serious and non-serious reactions. Some cases involved gastrointestinal problems, while others included more severe medical concerns. Reported figures have included suspected links to more than 200 deaths across these medicines. However, healthcare experts stress that a report to the Yellow Card system does not mean a medicine has been confirmed as the cause. The MHRA Yellow Card Scheme allows patients, healthcare workers, carers, and family members to report suspected side effects from medicines. The system helps regulators identify possible safety signals and monitor medicines after they become widely available. Why Weight Loss Jab Reports Are Being Closely Monitored The popularity of weight loss injections has increased significantly in recent years. Millions of prescriptions have been issued globally, and the growing number of users naturally means more side effect reports may be submitted. The MHRA has stated that reports must be viewed in the context of the large number of people using GLP-1 medicines. Increased awareness, wider use, and improved reporting can all affect the number of cases recorded. These medications work by affecting hormones involved in hunger, digestion, and blood sugar control. While they can help people lose weight, they can also cause side effects, especially when treatment begins or when doses are increased. Medical professionals usually recommend gradually adjusting doses and monitoring patients throughout treatment to reduce risks. Common Side Effects of Weight Loss Injections Like all prescription medicines, weight loss injections can cause side effects. Many reactions are temporary and improve as the body adjusts. Commonly reported side effects include: Nausea Vomiting Diarrhoea Constipation Stomach discomfort Indigestion Reduced appetite Digestive symptoms are among the most frequently reported reactions because these medicines slow digestion and influence appetite signals. Some patients may experience stronger reactions, especially after increasing their dosage. Anyone experiencing persistent or severe symptoms should contact a healthcare professional. Serious Risks Patients Should Know About Although many people use weight loss injections without major problems, some serious risks have been reported. Possible serious complications may include: Pancreatitis Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas and has been highlighted as a rare potential risk linked to GLP-1 medicines. Symptoms may include severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Kidney Problems Some patients have reported kidney-related issues, although these reactions are considered uncommon. Severe vomiting or dehydration may increase risks for some individuals. Blood Sugar Changes People using diabetes medications alongside weight loss injections may need monitoring because blood sugar levels can become too low in certain situations. Vision Changes Some patients have reported vision problems, particularly where blood sugar levels change rapidly. Patients should always discuss their personal health history with a doctor before starting treatment. Experts Say Benefits Must Be Balanced Against Risks Health authorities and manufacturers continue to state that GLP-1 medicines can provide significant benefits when prescribed appropriately. The MHRA has said that current evidence supports the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists when they are taken according to approved guidelines. Regulators continue to review safety information and update recommendations when necessary. Manufacturers of these medicines have also emphasized that patient safety remains a priority and that suspected side effects should be reported through official monitoring systems. What Patients Taking Weight Loss Jabs Should Do People currently using medicines such as Mounjaro or Wegovy should not stop treatment without speaking to a healthcare professional. Patients should: Follow the prescribed dosage instructions Attend medical check-ups when advised Report unusual or severe symptoms Seek urgent medical help for severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, or other worrying symptoms Weight loss medicines are not suitable for everyone. Doctors consider factors such as medical history, existing conditions, and other medications before prescribing them. Growing Demand for Weight Loss Treatments The rise of weight loss injections reflects a wider shift in how obesity is treated. These medicines have provided a new option for people who previously struggled to lose weight through lifestyle changes alone. However, their rapid growth has also increased the importance of careful prescribing, patient education, and long-term monitoring. As more people use these treatments, regulators will continue collecting safety information to better understand their benefits and risks. Conclusion Reports involving Mounjaro, Wegovy, and other weight loss injections have highlighted the importance of medicine safety monitoring. While thousands of suspected reactions have been recorded, these reports do not automatically mean the medicines caused every serious outcome. For many patients, weight loss injections may offer meaningful health benefits when used under medical supervision. However, understanding possible side effects and seeking professional advice remains essential. Anyone considering or currently taking weight loss medication should have open conversations with their healthcare provider and report any concerning symptoms promptly. Source MHRA Yellow Card Scheme data and published coverage from UK media outlets, including analysis of adverse reaction reports involving Mounjaro, Wegovy, and other GLP-1 weight loss medicines. Medical Disclaimer This article is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice. Weight loss medicines should only be used under the guidance of a qualified healthcare professional. If you experience severe or unusual symptoms while taking any medication, seek medical advice immediately.

title: Ready to Teach English Online? Here's How 51Talk Helps You Succeed from Day One
summary: Ready to teach English online? Discover how 51Talk training, resources, and support help you build communication skills and succeed from day one.
body_text: Teaching Techniques Aug 18, 2026 Ready to Teach English Online? Here's How 51Talk Helps You Succeed from Day One Ready to teach English online? Discover how 51Talk training, resources, and support help you build communication skills and succeed from day one. Starting something new often comes with questions. Am I ready to teach English online? How can I keep learners engaged through a screen? What if I need help improving my teaching skills? And how can I communicate clearly when teaching learners from different backgrounds and English levels? At 51Talk, you do not have to figure everything out on your own. From preparation and training to teaching resources and ongoing support, 51Talk helps online English teachers build the skills and confidence they need to deliver engaging online lessons. At the heart of that journey is one essential superpower: communication . Because when you teach English online, clear communication does more than help you explain a lesson. It helps you connect with learners, make English easier to understand, encourage participation, and create meaningful learning experiences from your first online lesson onward. Why Communication Is Your Greatest Online Teaching Superpower A learner knows the answer but hesitates to speak. Another understands the words on the screen but needs help putting them together. Sometimes, a simple question is met with silence. What happens next can define the learning experience. An effective online English teacher knows when to slow down, when to explain something differently, when to ask another question, and when to simply give a learner a little more time to find the words. That is why teaching English online is about more than grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation. English proficiency gives you the knowledge to teach, but strong communication helps you turn that knowledge into understanding, participation, and eventually, confidence. A clear instruction can help a learner know what to do next. The right question can encourage someone to speak. A gesture or visual cue can make a difficult word easier to understand. Positive feedback can give a hesitant learner enough confidence to try again. These moments may seem small, but together they can transform how a learner experiences English. And communication is a skill teachers can continue developing throughout their teaching journey. Turn English Proficiency Into Teaching Ability Knowing English and knowing how to help someone learn English are different abilities. Online teaching adds another dimension. Teachers need to communicate through a screen, guide the flow of a lesson, use digital teaching materials effectively, and keep learners actively participating. This is where preparation matters. 51Talk provides training designed to help teachers develop practical online teaching skills, from delivering clear instructions and adjusting speaking pace to providing corrections, asking purposeful questions, and encouraging learner participation. The goal is not simply to memorize teaching techniques. It is to understand when and how to use them. Imagine asking a question and seeing that a learner does not understand. Instead of repeating the same words, you simplify the question, change your pace, add a gesture, or give an example. Then the learner responds. That ability to adjust is where English proficiency begins turning into effective teaching. Create Online Lessons Learners Want to Join Once the lesson begins, communication becomes the experience. Teachers constantly make small decisions: when to move forward, when to pause, when to correct, when to encourage another attempt, and when a learner needs a different explanation. 51Talk provides structured teaching materials that give teachers a foundation for navigating these moments. With lesson content available during teaching sessions, teachers can focus more attention on delivery, learner engagement, pacing, pronunciation, and understanding. Over time, something else begins to happen. Teachers start discovering their own teaching style. Some bring energy through expressive gestures and voice variation. Others create an encouraging environment through patience and thoughtful questions. Some become particularly skilled at turning difficult concepts into simple explanations. There is no single personality that defines an effective online English teacher. What matters is the ability to recognize what a learner needs and adjust accordingly. Because the goal is not to speak more. It is to communicate better . Turn Participation Into Confidence A successful online lesson should not leave the learner simply listening. Learners need opportunities to answer, question, think, make mistakes, try again, and eventually express ideas independently. Communication makes those opportunities possible. A teacher might use Total Physical Response (TPR), facial expressions, visual cues, examples, voice variation, or positive reinforcement to make meaning clearer and participation easier. Consider a learner struggling with an unfamiliar word. Repeating the definition may not be enough. But pairing a simpler explanation with a gesture or example could create the moment when understanding finally clicks. The learner tries the word. The teacher provides guidance. The learner tries again. This time, it comes more confidently. That is more than completing part of a lesson. It is a learner experiencing what it feels like to understand, participate, improve, and succeed. When moments like these happen consistently, confidence begins to grow. Keep Growing with Every Lesson Teachers develop through experience, too. One lesson may reveal that an instruction could be shorter. Another might show that a learner needs a slower pace. A quiet learner may challenge a teacher to ask better questions, while a difficult concept may inspire a more creative way of explaining it. Each experience becomes an opportunity to become more effective. 51Talk supports continued teacher development through coaching, learning resources, and opportunities to strengthen online teaching capabilities. That ongoing development matters because strong communication is never really finished. Teachers continue learning how to listen more carefully, explain more clearly, respond more effectively, and adapt to different learners. The more these abilities develop, the more naturally teachers can create learning experiences that encourage learners to participate and communicate. And that is where teacher development connects directly to learner impact. When a Great Lesson Creates Greater Value For a learner, the value of an English lesson is not simply reaching the final page. It is what the learner can do because of the experience. Perhaps a learner who once answered with a single word begins constructing complete sentences. Someone who hesitated starts volunteering answers. A learner who needed constant guidance gradually becomes comfortable expressing an idea independently. These changes may happen one lesson at a time, but together they represent something much bigger. Clear communication creates understanding. Understanding encourages participation. Participation creates opportunities to practice. With consistent practice and guidance, learners can build both ability and confidence. That is how teacher quality becomes learner value. The lesson may happen online, but the confidence developed through it can go much further. Help Learners Speak Up, Stand Out, and Succeed This is what makes communication such a powerful teaching superpower. It allows a teacher to take knowledge and make it understandable, take hesitation and turn it into participation, and help learners gradually transform practice into confidence. For teachers beginning their journey, that ability does not need to be perfect on the first day. It develops through preparation, support, experience, and the willingness to keep learning from every lesson. Your first lessons may teach you how to give clearer instructions. The next may challenge you to become a better listener. Over time, you may discover the teaching style that allows you to connect most effectively with learners. And somewhere in that journey, a learner may begin speaking more confidently because you found the right way to reach them. That is the opportunity behind teaching English online with 51Talk: to continue developing as a teacher while helping learners develop the communication skills and confidence to speak up, stand out, and succeed Start Teaching with 51Talk and turn your communication skills into meaningful learner impact. Ready to teach online? Start teaching with 51Talk Back to Stories Read Next Story

title: Immutable Ledgers Explained: How Append-Only Data Models Work
summary: Learn how immutable ledgers use append-only writes, hash chaining, and compensating postings to preserve financial history.
body_text: In February 2016, cyber criminals tried to make fraudulent transfers totaling $951 million using malware inside Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT terminal. By the time investigators reconstructed the sequence, $81 million had left the bank's account, and the local database that should have shown the truth had been edited to hide it. This is the type of attack that an immutable ledger is built to prevent. An immutable ledger is a financial record where every posting is written once, ordered by sequence, cryptographically linked to the postings before it, and never altered or deleted after commit. Corrections can only happen as new postings are appended later in the sequence, so the full history remains reconstructable by anyone holding the raw log. When payment rails, partner banks, and internal systems disagree, the only defense is a record that cannot be quietly rewritten. It is an ordered, replayable history of every posting, preserved for auditors, operators, finance, and compliance teams. The case for immutability starts with what a mutable ledger cannot do, no matter how carefully it is instrumented. Why mutable ledgers cannot preserve financial history A mutable ledger shows whatever the most privileged process last wrote, which may have nothing to do with what actually happened. Three issues highlight why mutable ledgers cannot preserve financial records: adversarial edits to the underlying database, routine in-place updates from application code, and soft-delete patterns that regulators explicitly reject. Adversarial edits to the underlying database The Bangladesh Bank attackers understood this precisely. Custom malware intercepted SWIFT confirmation messages and rewrote the local database so that the fraudulent transfers never appeared in balance reports or reconciliation queries. Because the client-side database accepted in-place edits from a sufficiently privileged process, the malware could delete evidence of the fraudulent instructions, adjust balances to hide the missing $81 million, and suppress the printer output that would have alerted operators. No breach of SWIFT's central network was required because a mutable ledger gives any attacker who reaches it the same power the application has, to overwrite history so the record and reality diverge with no artifact left behind. In-place UPDATEs from application code Malice is not required for the same failure. The most common case is a balance column updated in place by application code: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 42; The statement is atomic, cheap, and indistinguishable from any other write. It also destroys the sequence of postings that produced the new balance: the prior value is gone, no row records the increment, and nothing links the change to the business event that caused it. If the balance later turns out to be wrong, from a duplicate credit or a race between two writers, there is no artifact to replay. The same failure hides behind ORM save-back patterns and admin-panel "edit balance" buttons that let support agents adjust totals directly. Soft deletes and updated_at timestamps Soft deletes and updated_at timestamps do not restore overwritten ledger history. A soft delete is an UPDATE that sets a flag, which means the same write path that flips the flag can silently alter any other field in the row. An updated_at column records only when the last write happened, not what it replaced. The prior value is not preserved, and successive writes overwrite the timestamp itself, so a row modified ten times looks identical to one modified once. Neither pattern gives an auditor a way to reconstruct what the record used to say. Regulators have already ruled on the pattern. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC's) amendments to Rule 17a-4, effective May 3, 2023, require broker-dealer records to be kept either in write once, read many (WORM) format or in a system that permits recreation of an original record if it is modified or deleted, alongside a complete time-stamped record of all modifications. A table that stores only final state plus a timestamp cannot recreate an original, so it fails that test by construction. How immutable ledgers preserve financial history Immutable ledgers close each of the failures in a mutable ledger with three combined mechanisms: 1 Append-only writes refuse in-place edits, so no UPDATE path exists to overwrite history. 2 Hash chaining links every posting to the one before it, so any change to a historical record breaks the chain and surfaces on the next verification pass. 3 Four invariants that turn the tamper-evident log into a record an auditor can reconstruct without trusting the application that wrote it. Each of those mechanisms rests on a specific structural property of the underlying store, starting with what "append-only" means at the data layer. What does "append-only" mean at the data layer? Append-only storage accepts new records only at the tail of the log and offers no write path to overwrite, modify, or physically delete an existing record. It is an ordered, immutable sequence of records that is continually appended to, where each record's offset fixes both its content and its position. A record's position matters because a commit log captures facts, such as events that happened at a given point in time. An append-only structure does not guarantee permanent immutability. Apache Kafka discards records after a configurable retention period , and PostgreSQL's multiversion concurrency control (MVCC) keeps old row versions after an UPDATE until VACUUM eventually reclaims dead tuples , so old versions can still be removed. An append-only interface also depends on the permissions enforcing it; a process with sufficient operating system (OS) privileges can still truncate or overwrite the underlying storage. For stronger immutability guarantees, enforcement has to sit beyond the log structure itself. Append-only and immutable differ. Append-only describes the structural property of the write path, while immutability describes the system-level guarantee that written data cannot be altered or deleted. The structure delivers the guarantee only when access control on the write path prevents every process, including privileged ones, from updating an existing record, or when cryptographic chaining makes any such update detectable. How hash chaining turns an append-only log into a tamper-evident record Hash chaining makes tampering detectable by construction. Each new posting stores a cryptographic hash computed from its own data combined with the previous posting's hash. Modify any historical record and its hash changes, which invalidates the chain hash stored in every subsequent record. An attacker who alters posting n must recompute every hash from n to the current head, and that recomputed head will not match any digest stored or distributed independently. Verification then depends on a digest that represents the ledger's history as of a point in time. Where the chain is enforced determines who it protects against. Formance Ledger uses hash chaining to make transaction history tamper-evident. Database-level protections defend against application bugs. A machine administrator with direct storage access can still bypass database checks and tamper with underlying files, but detection hinges on where digests are stored. Mechanism The adversarial condition where it breaks Database ledger tables (append-only at the application programming interface (API) level) Ledger verification detects tampering by recomputing hashes and comparing them with database digests; to preserve that tamper evidence, digests should be stored in protected external storage with immutability controls. Database ledger with external digest storage A privileged user can redirect or replace digest storage with unprotected storage, which can undermine tamper detection if verification does not inspect the digest locations. WORM immutable tables without hash chaining Any privileged actor with direct storage access; access controls alone do not provide cryptographic tamper evidence. Managed ledger journal The central trusted authority itself; the service operator sits outside the stated threat model. Hash chain enforced at the ledger layer, keys outside the database Requires compromising both database storage and the application-held key material. A database administrator (DBA) who edits storage files under a ledger-layer chain cannot make tampering pass integrity checks when verification is run against previously generated digests, so the tampering surfaces on the next verification pass. Every database-layer alternative in the table collapses to a single question, what we can call the digest-reachability test : can the attacker reach the digests too? Four invariants immutable ledgers must enforce A tamper-evident log becomes a trustworthy financial ledger only when four invariants hold at write time: gapless sequence ordering, zero-sum postings, non-destructive correction, and independent verifiability. 1. Gapless sequence numbers Every ledger posting must carry a sequence number that increases without gaps, because replaying the sequence then exposes every class of positional tampering. Replay detects missing records and positional tampering. Any issue exposes a missing record, and duplicate or lower-than-current sequence numbers expose insertion at an existing position or backdating. Sequence allocators can fail here if numbers are allocated before commit. A rolled-back transaction can leave a permanent gap that only becomes visible under concurrency. Wall-clock timestamps cannot substitute for sequence numbers either. 2. Zero-sum balance across postings Double-entry accounting requires every posting to net to zero across all accounts, which turns tampering into an arithmetic alarm. Every movement of value records a source and a destination. An injected or altered record that lacks a perfectly matching counter-entry pushes the sum of all postings away from zero. The deviation surfaces on any balance verification pass regardless of how the record was changed. Use layered checks because the application can assert before commit. In contrast, the database can use a CHECK constraint requiring each entry to be strictly a debit or a credit. An asynchronous audit job can scan for transactions whose lines fail to sum to zero. 3. Non-destructive correction Corrections must be appended as new compensating postings, ideally linked to the original posting, so both the error and its resolution remain immutable, ordered facts in the log. Event sourcing treats undoing a change as a new compensating event, while the original event remains unchanged. In Numscript , a purpose-built language for describing financial transactions, a wrong $2,500.00 fee posted against customer 1234 looks like this: // Original (incorrect) fee posting send [USD/2 250000] ( source = @customers:1234:wallet destination = @platform:revenue:fees ) set_tx_meta ( "event_type" , "fee_charge" ) set_tx_meta ( "fee_id" , "fee1234" ) The correction is a new posting appended later in the sequence, moving the same amount back and referencing the original by ID: // Compensating posting, appended with a reference to the original send [USD/2 250000] ( source = @platform:revenue:fees destination = @customers:1234:wallet ) set_tx_meta ( "event_type" , "fee_reversal" ) set_tx_meta ( "reversal_id" , "rev1234" ) set_tx_meta ( "adjusted_posting_event_id" , "fee1234" ) Both postings are immutable, sequenced entries. The net effect on balances is zero, and the history explains why: a charge happened, then a correction happened. Bi-temporality, tracking both valid and transaction time, keeps the correction from distorting history. The compensating posting carries a recorded timestamp of today while its effective timestamp matches the original charge, so point-in-time queries before the correction return the original state and queries after return the corrected state. 4. Independent verifiability The log must be verifiable without trusting the application layer that wrote it. An auditor holding only the raw log and its hash chain can recompute every chain hash and replay the postings to confirm integrity, and can confirm balances if the log contains all information needed to derive them without additional application state. Regulators are converging on this exact demand for reconstruction. The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) requires crypto-asset service providers to arrange for records to be kept. Those records must cover all services, orders, and transactions sufficient to allow competent authorities to fulfill their supervisory tasks, and must be retained for five years. The Financial Conduct Authority's (FCA's) Client Assets Sourcebook (CASS) 15 safeguarding rules are in force from 7 May 2026. They require records to be maintained to demonstrate "their correspondence to the relevant funds held for clients." Each framework asks the same architectural question: can you prove history from the record itself? Benefits of an immutable ledger for financial infrastructure Immutable ledgers give you a financial record you can prove from the raw log, without trusting the application that wrote it. Every posting is a permanent, hash-anchored fact, and provider confirmations, reversals, and reconciliations arrive as new appended entries rather than edits to settled history. Formance Ledger delivers these properties natively: hash-chained transactions, immutable, tamper-evident entries once posted, programmatically enforced double-entry accounting, and bi-temporality that supports point-in-time views and backdated corrections without rewriting history. The decision in front of you is whether to keep building bespoke verification infrastructure around a database that permits the exact writes your auditors prohibit, or to run a ledger that treats immutability as a structural guarantee.

title: Fake Loan Apps in India 2026: Full List, RBI Bans & How to Stay Safe
summary: Stay away from loan scams. Check the full fake loan apps list for India 2026, the tactics fraud apps use, RBI action so far, and how to verify any app.
body_text: Fake Loan Apps in India 2026: Full List, RBI Bans & How to Stay Safe A fake loan app doesn't steal from you the day you install it. It waits. First comes the instant approval, then the tiny disbursal, then the impossible charges, and finally the recovery calls to your family using the contacts it copied on day one. This guide gives you a researched fake loan apps list for 2026, shows you exactly how these scams operate, and hands you a two-minute verification routine that works on any app. If you'd rather start from the safe side, apps distributed through the GroMo app lend only through RBI-regulated entities. Key Takeaways Fake loan apps profit from your data and panic, not your interest payments. Contact list access is their main weapon. The RBI has had hundreds of unauthorised lending apps removed from Indian app stores, and the cleanup is ongoing. No genuine lender asks for money before disbursal. An upfront fee demand ends the conversation. Popular apps like Kissht, Moneyview, mPokket, PayRupik, Ring and Buddy Loan are legitimate, RBI-linked platforms that scammers often imitate with lookalike names. Verify any app against the RBI's Digital Lending Apps directory before installing, and report fraud on the RBI's Sachet portal. Table of contents What Makes a Loan App Fake? Fake Loan Apps List in India 2026 How Fake Instant Loan App Scams Work Red Flags Before You Install RBI Bans and Government Action How to Verify Any Loan App in Two Minutes Trapped Already? Do This Now FAQs What Makes a Loan App Fake? A fake loan app is any lending app with no RBI-regulated bank or NBFC behind it. That single missing piece changes everything, because an unregulated app answers to nobody. There's no grievance officer, no fair recovery code, no Key Fact Statement, and no legal cap on what it charges. Some fake apps never lend at all. They harvest your Aadhaar, PAN, bank details and phone contacts, then sell that data or use it for extortion. Others lend small amounts quickly to build trust, then bury you in hidden charges that never appear in writing. The name of the app tells you nothing. Scammers routinely copy the look, icon and name of genuine apps, which is why a fake personal loan app list can never fully replace verification. The doubt reaches genuine platforms too, which is why we've answered is GroMo real or fake head on. Learn the check once and you're protected from apps that haven't even launched yet. Despite careful checking, an entry may become outdated or contain an error. If you find any incorrect information here, please contact us and we'll verify and fix or remove it promptly. How Fake Instant Loan App Scams Work The scam follows the same script almost every time. The hook. You see an ad or SMS promising an instant loan with no credit check and guaranteed approval. Genuine lenders never guarantee approval. The permissions grab. During installation, the app demands access to your contacts, photos and SMS. This is the real product. Your data is worth more to them than your EMIs. The fee or the micro-loan. Either the app demands a processing fee before disbursal and vanishes with it, or it disburses a small amount so you feel committed. The impossible bill. Charges appear that were never in writing, because there was never a Key Fact Statement or a loan agreement to begin with. The harassment. When you dispute the amount, recovery agents call your family and colleagues using the copied contact list, often with morphed photos and threats. Every fake instant loan app list entry above ran some version of this playbook. The details change, the script doesn't. Red Flags Before You Install No named RBI-registered bank or NBFC anywhere on the app page or website. The app arrives as a link on WhatsApp or SMS instead of an official app store. It demands contact list and gallery access before showing you a single offer. Any request for money before disbursal, whatever it's called. Guaranteed approval with no credit check. No grievance officer, no support email, no registered office address. Countdown timers pressuring you to accept in minutes. One red flag is enough. Close the page and move on. RBI Bans and Government Action The cleanup is real and ongoing. Working with Google and app store operators, the RBI and the government have had hundreds of unauthorised lending apps taken down from Indian app stores, and the RBI now maintains a Digital Lending Apps directory that maps legitimate apps to their regulated lenders. The RBI also runs the Sachet portal where anyone can report an unauthorised lending entity directly to the regulator. Complaints filed there feed the takedown pipeline, so reporting a fake app genuinely helps the next borrower. Takedowns can't end the problem alone, because removed apps relaunch under new names within weeks. That's why verification beats memorising any list. How to Verify Any Loan App in Two Minutes Find the lending partner's name on the app's Play Store listing or website. No named lender means uninstall. Search that lender in the RBI's NBFC register and the Digital Lending Apps directory on the RBI website. Open the Key Fact Statement before accepting any offer. It must show the full annualised cost in one number. Confirm disbursal goes directly to your bank account, never through a wallet or an agent. Check the permissions screen. KYC needs your documents, not your contact list. This is the same routine we used to build our list of RBI approved loan apps . Trapped Already? Do This Now Cut the access first. Revoke all the app's permissions in your phone settings, then uninstall. Change your banking passwords and UPI PIN immediately. Don't pay threats. Amounts invented outside a written agreement have no legal standing. Paying once marks you as someone who pays. Document everything. Screenshots of chats, call recordings, payment records. Evidence turns your complaint from a story into a case. Report on three channels. The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at cybercrime.gov.in or the 1930 helpline, the RBI's Sachet portal, and your local police station with your documentation. Warn your contacts. Tell family and colleagues they may receive calls, and that they should ignore them. Taking the surprise away takes most of the scammers' power. FAQs Is there an official fake loan apps list from the RBI? The RBI publishes the opposite: a directory of legitimate digital lending apps mapped to regulated lenders. Any lending app missing from that directory and lacking a named RBI-registered lender should be treated as unsafe. What happens if I don't repay a fake loan app? Amounts demanded outside a written loan agreement have no legal standing, and a fake app can't report you to credit bureaus. Their only weapon is harassment, which is itself a crime you should report on cybercrime.gov.in or the 1930 helpline. Can fake loan apps access my contacts after I uninstall them? They keep whatever data they copied while installed, which is why speed matters. Revoke permissions, uninstall, change your passwords and warn your contacts the same day. How do fake apps get on official app stores? They launch as harmless-looking apps, pass automated review, then switch on the lending scam through server-side changes. Stores remove them once reported, which is why new names keep appearing. Kissht is real or fake? Kissht is real. It lends through RBI-registered NBFC partners and is distributed on established platforms including GroMo's catalogue. Watch out for lookalike apps misusing the Kissht name, and install only from the official store listing. Moneyview is real or fake? Moneyview is real. It operates with Whizdm Finance and RBI-registered lending partners including Aditya Birla Finance, with transparent fee disclosure before you accept an offer. mPokket is real or fake? mPokket is real. It's the consumer brand of Mpokket Financial Services Private Limited, an NBFC registered with the RBI, focused on small loans for students and young professionals. PayRupik fake or real? PayRupik is real. It's operated by Sayyam Investments Private Limited, an RBI-registered NBFC. As with any small-ticket lender, read the Key Fact Statement carefully before accepting. Ring loan app fake or real? Ring is real. It lends through RBI-regulated entities and is distributed through established channels including GroMo's catalogue. Verify you're installing the official app, not a clone. Buddy Loan app is real or fake? Buddy Loan is real. It works as a loan marketplace that connects borrowers to RBI-registered banks and NBFCs rather than lending itself. The loan you get comes from a regulated lender on its panel. Disclaimer: This article is compiled through human research from authentic public sources for general awareness. App names, ownership and status change frequently. If you spot any incorrect or outdated information, please contact us and we'll correct or remove it promptly. Always verify a lender on the RBI website before borrowing. This isn't financial or legal advice. Get the GroMo App

title: Why Blockchain Matters
summary: Blockchain became famous because of the cryptocurrency Bitcoin. The use of investing in blockchain technology is expected to grow.
body_text: Blockchain became famous because of the cryptocurrency Bitcoin. The use of investing in blockchain technology is expected to grow. Spending is expected to reach more than $4 billion in 2020 , which is still a nearly 58% increase over 2019, despite the coronavirus pandemic reducing estimates, according to the International Data Corporation , a market intelligence company. And in the next three years the spending is projected to grow to about $14 billion. Here’s how blockchain works and why it matters. What is blockchain? Essentially, blockchain is a decentralized database that people crowdsource. GoDirect Trade is an ecommerce marketplace for used airplane parts that relies on blockchain. Think about it ike a scoreboard at a sports game. Everyone knows the score because everyone can see the score on the scoreboard. Blockchain works the same way because everyone has a copy of the database. Ultimately, that provides transparency. It helps manufacture trust between two parties. “You can never delete a record, so it’s a technology that is highly secure and open source. Real-world application: Used Airplane Parts The used airplane parts industry is a $4 billion industry and less than 2% of that business is conducted online. That presented an opportunity for ecommerce of the used parts. GoDirect Trade is an online marketplace that allows sellers to list their parts online for a yearly subscription fee. But how do you guarantee pedigree of those parts that can average prices in the five-digits? Enter: Blockchain. Buyers can review the ledger and see the history of the part. That also helps address safety concerns for pieces critical to flying an airplane. For new parts manufactured by Honeywell, the ledger will start fresh like a digital birth certificate. Decades from now, every Honeywell part will have a record of the planes it has been in or repairs made to it. The Future of Blockchain The used airplane parts business is just one-way blockchain technology can be used. Industries leveraging blockchain have barely scratched the surface. For example, blockchain could track a piece of produce from the moment it is picked to when it lands on a dinner table. And the guaranteed security of transactions will revolutionize industries.
